text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.4.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Launch modeling and Part A Pulse Check, students use the words around unfamiliar terms like phenomenon and drought to infer meaning, and then apply the same context-clue strategy to circled words in their assigned paragraphs."},{"code":"RI.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Part A students underline 3-4 facts from their paragraph, and in Part B the prediction posters require quoted evidence with each inference, beginning 'Because the text says ___, stories might explain ___.'"},{"code":"RI.6.7","verdict":"not-taught","reason":"The lesson deliberately restricts students to 'no pictures, only words' and never has them integrate information from a visual, quantitative, or other media format with the text; the only mention is a teacher note deferring this to later lessons."},{"code":"RI.6.9","verdict":"partly","reason":"In the Part B gallery walk, students compare predictions and the texts' general focus, but they never compare how different authors present the same events or subject, since each group reads a different topic-level excerpt."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"Part A assigns one teacher-selected paragraph from each of the three named Newsela texts, so all three texts the Outline names are used, though the Outline's page references are not specified."}}
